resources.string: A chart of other tools\' entries and of variables, drawn and never computed: a subset of Vega-Lite (layer, vconcat, hconcat, concat, facet, repeat; marks line, point, bar, area, text, arc, tick, rect; encoding channels) whose data come from a source per layer, never written in the config: a tool\'s entries, or a grid reading variables and field readings at each step of the displayed period. A total per day is a grid column, never an aggregate. Colors are palette names. Keeps no entries of its own.
Your entries and figures drawn as lines, bars, pies or calendars
the moment the chart is shown

How the views are laid out, Vega-Lite\'s: layer (one view, its layers over one another), vconcat, hconcat or concat (several views, each {\"title\"?, \"layer\"}, one above the other, side by side, or wrapped every columns), facet (a small view per value of facet.field), repeat (a small view per field of repeat, the channels whose field is \"repeat\" taking it). Nothing else composes: no data, no title, no width.
The column whose values each get a small view; the layers that do not have it are drawn whole in each
A column each small view takes in turn, where a channel\'s field is \"repeat\"
How many small views stand side by side, 1 by default: a phone is narrow
What the layer shows, a few words for the form

Where the layer\'s rows come from, in place of Vega-Lite\'s data: the string "entries" or "grid", what it reads (selection; step and columns) being keys of the layer beside it. entries: a row per entry of one tool in the period (selection), its columns timestamp, name and its fields by path (data.value, extra.mood). grid: a row per step of the period, read at the end of the step, its columns timestamp (the step\'s start), weekday (1 for Monday to 7), week (the day its week starts), and one per column read.
The calendar step a row stands for, with the day start and week start set in the app
The column\'s name, which channels write in field: letters, digits and _, not timestamp, weekday, week or repeat
Without a period, it reads its step
Columns turned into rows: a row per row and column, the column\'s name under the first name of as, its value under the second; of one sort (kcal with kcal). Vega-Lite\'s fold
A fold\'s two new columns, a key then a value; key and value by default
Multiple choices spread into a row per option. Vega-Lite\'s flatten
linear by default; step-after holds each value until the next, a level that changes in steps; monotone smooths without overshooting
Lengths drawn then left, in dp, [4, 4] for a dashed limit
The points\' shape, a circle by default
Vega-Lite\'s mark, always an object {\"type\", ...}. A threshold is a variable drawn as a line, never a rule
The measured values show on the line
A point\'s area in square dp, 30 by default
A filled point; hollow by default
The column of the row the channel shows, by its name; \"repeat\" in a repeat
Vega-Lite\'s type, the column\'s own by default: quantitative for a number or a duration, temporal for a date, nominal for a choice or a text; ordinal orders categories
Shown at the bottom unless false
Required on bars and areas split by a category: none lays them over one another, zero piles them up, normalize brings each place to a hundred percent
A point\'s area for every row, in square dp
The opacity of every row, from 0 to 1
A palette name for every row
Two fixed bounds, [min, max]; a value past them is marked at the edge, never drawn against it
Whether the scale includes zero, as Vega-Lite does by default for a quantity
Bounds rounded to graduations, by default
The scale runs the other way
Lines across the chart at each graduation; on the left vertical axis by default
The side of the vertical axis, left by default: another unit goes to the right, with its own scale
The categories in the order they take the colors of range
Palette names the categories take in turn; for a quantity, the colors of its two ends
The variable of column %1$s cannot be read.
Column %1$s reads %2$s, which its tool no longer has.
Column %1$s reads a variable or a field of a tool, never a value written: a threshold is a variable.
A grid steps from the start of the period shown: it needs one.
%1$s names %2$s, a column the layer does not give. It gives: %3$s.
%1$s cannot name a column: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit.
%1$s is a column every row of a grid already has (%2$s): name yours otherwise.
A fold puts its columns on one axis: %1$s and %2$s are not of one sort.
A flatten spreads a multiple choice: %1$s is none.
The channel %1$s shows nothing: give it a field or a value, or remove it.
The bounds of %1$s are two numbers, [min, max].
The channel %1$s goes with an arc (or a text on one), not with a %2$s.
Only bars and areas stack, not a %1$s.
These %1$s are split by a category: say how they stack in stack on their value\'s channel (%2$s).
The condition of %1$s puts a column of the row on its left.
The condition of %1$s: %2$s does not compare %3$s.
The condition of %1$s compares %2$s and %3$s, which are not of one type.
The condition of %1$s compares with a column of the row or a value written: a variable is read as a column of a grid.
The layers of a view share their horizontal axis: %1$s and %2$s put different sorts of values there.
%1$s and %2$s share a vertical axis but not a unit: put one on the %3$s (axis.orient).
Nothing to draw in this period.
Touch a mark to see its values.
A fold names its two columns in as, a key then a value: [\"key\", \"value\"].
A transform is a fold or a flatten, one of the two.
%1$s: %2$s is not a value this channel takes.
Cannot be drawn: open it to see why
